Key insights

July cash flow on track
$324K of July's $363K booked is collected (89.2%), with $39K still expected within the month. By company: NoDig collects fastest (91.6%), RTM 89.4%, Unify360 trails at 84.1% — see Payments & Forecast above.
Contract mix improving
Contracted revenue (In Contract + Annual) reached 52.3% in June — first month above month-to-month — up from 37.4% in January. M2M fell $260K to $188K.
RTM concentration risk
RTM is 94.0% of booked revenue ($2.594M of $2.758M). Unify360 ($125.7K) and NoDig ($39.0K) stay small; any RTM cancellation spike hits the total directly.
Active campaigns declining
Active campaigns fell from 246 (Jan) to 219 (Jul MTD). June recovered to 230 before July resumed the slide.
Net recurring deficit
New recurring ($90.0K YTD) trails cancellations ($169.3K) by −$79.3K — every month except April ran a deficit.
Revenue holding near $400K/mo
Monthly booked held $388–416K through June (avg $399.0K); July is $363K MTD and firms up as billing completes.

Key insights

July is mid-month
89.2% of July's $363,277 booked has been collected so far, against 98.6% for June at close. Mid-month, not a collection problem — the figure to watch is the $39,293 still outstanding.
RTM concentration risk
RTM is 94.0% of booked revenue ($2.594M of $2.758M). Any acceleration in cancellations hits the total directly.
Recurring runs a deficit
New sales ($286.3K YTD) beat cancellations ($169.3K) by +$115.8K, but on recurring alone it's a −$79.3K deficit ($90.0K new recurring vs $169.3K cancelled).
Expansion softens but doesn't cover churn
Upgrades beat downgrades by +$42.4K YTD (existing accounts are growing), but that only partly offsets the −$79.3K recurring deficit — the recurring base is still net −$37.3K for the year.
Active campaigns declining
Active campaigns fell from 246 (Jan) to 219 (Jul MTD) — 11.0%, the clearest attrition signal.
Collection is healthy
96.6% of booked revenue is collected ($2.674M paid YTD); $84.7K outstanding — mostly July recurring, which clears as the month closes.

Madison leads profitability

Veronica carries the most attrition

Revenue retention — NRR & GRR · existing recurring book · Feb–Jul 2026

Retention KPIs
How much of last month’s recurring revenue we keep — before any new sales
Net Revenue Retention
95.8%
Feb–Jul average · after customer upgrades
Gross Revenue Retention
92.0%
Feb–Jul average · before upgrades
How to read this
  • Start a month with $100 of recurring revenue from customers we already have.
  • After cancellations and downgrades, $92 is left — that’s Gross Retention (92%).
  • Add back existing customers who upgraded and it’s about $96 — that’s Net Retention (96%).
  • Still under $100, so current customers slowly shrink recurring revenue on their own — new sales are what keep it growing.
  • Above 100% Net Retention, the book would grow even without a single new customer.

Key insights

Recurring base restated higher
On the 7-classification Billing Master basis, YTD recurring is $2.513M at 91.1% of booked — up from $2.22M under the old Recurring-only definition.
Recurring is holding and inching up
July recurring $333.0K, +1.3% vs June ($328.8K). RTM is the anchor at $311.6K; Unify360 ($16.9K) and NoDig ($4.6K) are small but steady.
Full-year forecast rises, not falls
The roll-forward lifts recurring from $333K (Jul) to $376K (Dec) — full-year recurring $4.30M and total revenue $4.67M — as growth-case new business outpaces the $10K/mo churn peg.
New business is the growth driver
~31.5% of each new deal lands as recurring (H1 share); Aug–Dec new business follows the 2026 Pipeline deck (Growth case).
Concentration in RTM
RTM is ~94% of recurring, so the trajectory tracks RTM. Diversification into Unify360 / NoDig would reduce single-entity dependence.
Churn is the key sensitivity
H1 churn averaged ~$24K/mo (June alone $58.1K) vs the $10K/mo peg the base case assumes. At the H1 run-rate, recurring ends the year at ~$307K and full-year recurring is ~$4.09M (−$213K) — shown as the red downside line.

EBITDA Analysis — Reference (Accounting-Based)

Reference view only · Mirrors the QuickBooks EBITDA figures (RTM) from the EBITDA (QuickBooks) tab, which remains the source of truth. Per that tab’s formula, EBITDA = (Sales − Operational Expense) + Interest + Payroll Taxes + Depreciation + Amortization; D&A = $0, so EBITDA sits above operating income by the payroll-tax & interest add-backs. QuickBooks closes with a lag, so only booked months appear.

Key insights

Paid base declining
Paid revenue fell from $413.9K (Jan) to $382.4K (Jun) — a $31.4K or 7.6% reduction over 6 months.
Outstanding improved in June
Outstanding dropped from $26.0K in May to $12.0K in June — a positive collection sign despite the cancel spike.
Campaigns billed down 6.5%
Unique campaigns billed fell from 246 (Jan) to 230 (Jun) — 16 campaigns lost in six months. July stands at 227, still filling.
Jun cancellations highest YTD
29 unique campaigns cancelled in June (74 billing lines) totalling $58,141 — the largest single-month cancel event of 2026.
ActionRoofing recovered in June
Bounced from just $330 in May back to $7,824 in June — monitoring needed but June shows recovery.
SEO is the top category
SEO drives $620.7K of paid billings YTD Jan–Jul (26.6% of total) — the single largest revenue category.

Key insights

Sales declining year over year
Total sales fell $6.51M (2023) → $5.89M (2025); 2026 YTD ($2.74M) tracks ~21% below 2025’s Jan–Jul pace.
GBP is the sharpest decline
GBP collapsed −59% ($1.63M → $673K, 2023→2025) — the single biggest drag on the service mix.
SEO remains the anchor
SEO is the #1 service every year and still the largest revenue driver — the stable core despite market softness.
Cancellations accelerating
2026 YTD cancellations ($169.3K) are +63% vs 2025 YTD ($103.8K) — the clearest risk signal in the book.
Attrition mix has shifted
The top cancellation service moved from GBP (2023–24) to SEO (2025–26) — churn now follows the largest service.
New sales more resilient
New sales fell ~1.2% YTD vs 2025 ($286.3K vs $289.0K prorated) — contraction is broad, not just recurring.

Annual summary — all years

EntityMetric20222023202420252026 YTDTrend
Formula: EBITDA = (Sales − Operational Expense) + Interest + Taxes (Payroll) + Depreciation + Amortization Sources: QuickBooks P&L (authoritative) — RTM per revised Profit & Loss, Jan–Jul 2026 (revised 7/22/2026); Unify360 per prior QB. Interest = QB "Interest Paid" (RTM) / "Interest Expense" (U360); payroll taxes & interest are added back per the formula; D&A = $0 (not recorded in QB). June 2026 restated: the $100K Home Rebuild and other owner/non-operating items were reclassified to "Other Expenses," lifting the June operating result. Dec figures (FY2022–2025) include QB year-end payroll tax true-up adjustments.

Key insights

RTM FY2023 was peak performance
$6.16M revenue and $2.52M EBITDA at 40.9% margin — the strongest year on record. The business demonstrated it can sustain 40%+ margins at scale.
FY2024–25 margin compression
RTM margins dropped to 30.5% (FY24) and 29.0% (FY25) due to cost growth outpacing revenue. FY2026 YTD is recovering strongly back to 40.4%.
U360 is recovering
U360 EBITDA improved from -$936K (FY23) → -$776K (FY24) → -$216K (FY25) → +$22K (positive) in FY26 YTD at 14.8% margin. The loss trajectory has fully reversed.
Combined story is positive
Combined EBITDA of ~$940K YTD Jan–Jul 2026 at 38.8% margin — annualizes to ~$1.88M, recovering toward the FY22–23 levels.
Dec true-ups distort monthly view
December figures each year include large payroll tax year-end adjustments. Use annual totals for trend analysis, not individual months.
D&A = $0 across all years
Neither RTM nor U360 records Depreciation or Amortization in QuickBooks. If a separate depreciation schedule exists, those figures can be added as ITDA components.

Key insights

OpEx down 16.1% Jan–Jun
Total operating expense fell from $216.8K (Jan) to $181.9K (Jun) — $1.204M YTD. Five consecutive months of decline before June.
Payroll is 79.9% of OpEx
At $962.7K of $1.204M YTD, payroll dominates the cost base. Card charges ($144.2K) are a distant second at 12.0%.
May's drop was card-driven, not payroll
The $25.0K May decline came 53% from card charges (−$13.3K, 43% below their 6-month average) and only 30% from payroll. June reversed it: card charges rebounded $10.0K, the first month-over-month OpEx increase (+$3.1K).
Payroll declining 15.6% Jan–Jun
Total payroll dropped from $171.7K (Jan) to $144.9K (Jun) — $962.7K YTD.
Executive = largest dept cost
At $32.6K/mo, executive overhead is the single largest department cost — 24.9% of the $131.1K monthly total.
PH payroll = 66.7% of total
PH team at $641.8K YTD (70 staff) vs. US at $320.9K (5 staff) — 2.0× the US spend. On June payroll over the current 75-person roster that is $1,433/mo per PH head vs. $8,914/mo per US head, a 6.2× unit-cost gap.
